**Triage: lands in `packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx` (the `detail-section` registration) and/or `DetailSection`; `domain:ui`; `priority:p2`.**

The block is registered with **flat** inputs (`title`, `description`, `fields`, …) while `DetailSection` reads `section.*` only. ⇒ an authored `detail-section` node hands the component `section === undefined`, so **every declared input is inert**. The registration and the component disagree about the shape of the same block.

⇒ p2 rather than p3: this is not one dropped key, it is the entire declared input surface of a registered block doing nothing — and the authoring surface advertises all of it. An author fills in `title`, `description` and `fields`, publishes clean, and gets nothing.

⚠️ **Two repairs exist and they are not equivalent — name the one you take in the PR:** teach the component to read the flat props, or change the registration to declare the nested `section` shape it actually reads. The second changes what authors may write; if the flat inputs have ever been authored anywhere, that is a compatibility question rather than a free choice. ⇒ **check for authored usages first** and say what you found; if any exist, stop and report rather than invalidating them.

⛔ Not in scope: objectui#6955's input value-vocabulary question, which the filing seat correctly kept separate.

`Size/model suggestion:` M.

## Ruling recorded — A: `detail-section` keeps its FLAT authoring surface; PR #9221 is the delivery and closes this card on merge (director seat, decision batch #118 item 1, 2026-09-12)

Maintainer, verbatim (live PM chat, 2026-09-12T02:2xZ), after asking 「协议是怎么约定的，类似主流平台是怎么设计的？」 and reading the seat's answer:

> A

### The reading the ruling rests on (measured on objectstack `origin/main`, 2026-09-12T02:1xZ)

- **The protocol models a section in exactly one shape: a container with flat attributes and a `fields` list.** `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` declares the record-details block's `sections: z.array(strictObject({ name, label, description, icon, columns, group, fields, hideEmpty, collapsible, defaultCollapsed, showBorder, headerColor }))`, and its own note says "one shape" — the earlier "section ID list" spelling was deleted for having no producer and no consumer, and the Studio block designer authors `{label, columns, fields}`. `FormSectionSchema` (`view.zod.ts:2724`) is the same shape for form views.
- **The protocol declares no standalone `detail-section` block.** It is this repo's own registration, authored only as a `detail-view` tab's `content` (README, and #6955's pin); under ADR-0082 the spec is the source of truth and the registry a designer subset, with divergence carried by the conformance ratchet.
- **Seven of the eight flat inputs are the protocol's section keys by name and meaning.** The one divergence is `title`: the protocol deliberately withholds `title` as a second spelling of the heading slot `label` (held on #11661 for the declare-vs-converge ruling).
- Mainstream platforms model a section the same way — Salesforce page-layout sections and Dynamic Forms field sections (label, columns, collapsible, plus child fields), Dataverse FormXML `<section>` attributes plus rows/cells, ServiceNow form sections — ⚠️ from the seat's memory, not verified against vendor documentation; none models a section as a component whose single input is a section object.

⇒ Under 「协议为准」: **A** (flat, as the protocol's section item) is the protocol's shape; **B** (a nested `section` input) would make the authoring surface mirror a component's internal prop and is not taken; **C** (retire) is not taken — the tab-content use has no protocol replacement and the surface has an authored site and a landed pin.

### Consequences, landed with the ruling

1. PR #9221 (green, not draft) is the delivery: the seam adapter folds the eight declared inputs into the `section` object; `DetailSection` and the declared `inputs` stay byte-identical. With the reserved product question answered, **nothing remains on this card after the merge** — the `domain:ui` seat merges and closes this card completed (⛔ the director seat merges nothing).
2. Carried, ⛔ not this PR's: the block's input vocabulary is to be DERIVED from the protocol's section item rather than hand-typed, and its `title` input follows #11661's ruling (converge to `label` or declare) — the seat notes it on #11661, no new card.

### State

`needs-user-decision` stripped; `pm:dispatched` and the assignee stay until the merge. `bug`-class labels unchanged.

## Closing — the card's own question was decided and implemented. Measured on `main`

⛔ **Not inherited from the PR.** My release note (2026-09-14T09:26Z) said this seat had not re-measured. I read PR objectui#9221 and measured at `origin/main` `bbc9dc3`.

### The card picked none of three dispositions. One was taken.

This card was explicit that it was **not pre-judging**, and listed three:

1. **Adapt at the seam** — fold the flat props into a `section` object, making the eight declared names true.
2. **Declare what the component takes** — replace the eight with one `section` input of `type: 'object'`.
3. **Retire the tag** under ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove.

⭐ **Disposition 1 was taken**, and the file says so at the registration itself (`packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx:340-352`):

> ⚠️ Against `DetailSectionNode`, **NOT** `DetailSection` — and that is what makes the `inputs` below true (objectui#8626).

`packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailSectionNode.tsx:112` is the adapter; `:101` declares `DETAIL_SECTION_NODE_INPUTS`, the eight names, as the single source the registration and the fold both read. Pinned by `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/detailSectionAuthoredNode-8626.test.tsx`.

### ⭐ The card's unexecuted half, executed

The card flagged one claim as a **reading rather than a measurement** and asked the taker not to believe it unexecuted:

> `DetailSection`'s first statement is `React.useState(section.defaultCollapsed ?? false)`. With `section` undefined that is a property read on `undefined`, i.e. a **throw** at first render … Whoever picks this up should execute it before believing that sentence.

PR objectui#9221 executed it. The in-file record: *"Bound directly, `section` arrived `undefined` and the very first `section.defaultCollapsed` read THREW — measured end to end, the author's page showed `SchemaErrorBoundary`'s orange 'failed to render' banner in place of the block."* ⇒ the card's suspicion was right, and it is now a measurement.

### ⭐ Why disposition 2 was NOT taken, which is the part worth keeping

The PR's reasoning, and this seat agrees with it: declaring a nested `section` object would have been the **cheaper declaration, not the truer contract**. `inputs` publishes what an **author** may write, and an author has never been able to write a `section` object here — the platform REFUSES the nested shape. Taking it would have silently broken the README example, objectui#6955's pin, and every authored page already written against the manifest.

### The residual, measured — and it is ONE member, not three

PR objectui#9221's acceptance notes recorded, as *"Noted, not filed"*, that the registration declares 8 of the 11 members `DetailViewSection` carries, with `name` / `icon` / `visible` undeclared. Re-measured here, with every **declared** member carried as a lit control in the same pass:

| `section.icon` | **2** reads | ⛔ undeclared |
|---|---|---|
| `section.name` | **0** | undeclared, and unread |
| `section.visible` | **0** | undeclared, and unread |

and the eight controls — `title` 4, `description` 4, `fields` 8, `collapsible` 2, `defaultCollapsed` 1, `columns` 1, `showBorder` 3, `headerColor` 2 — all non-zero in that same pass, so the two zeros are readings.

⇒ **only `icon`** is both read by the renderer and unreachable by an author. ⭐ Filed as **objectui#9529**, ⛔ filed BEFORE this comment cited it. It is a decision to **widen** a published authoring surface (clause ②), so it is ⛔ not folded in here and ⛔ not pre-judged there.

### Verdict

The defect this card names — *"every `detail-section` input is a FLAT prop the renderer never reads"* — is repaired, its three dispositions are settled by an executed measurement rather than a preference, and the two adjacent observations found along the way are filed separately (objectui#9218 for `showBorder`, objectui#9529 for `icon`). Nothing remains under this card's own title.

⇒ closed as completed, `pm:queue` stripped. PR objectui#9221 said `Part of #8626` because a dev seat never ends a card — the PM does.
